2.4 Function to save functions

write_function <- function(func_name, folder) {
  
  # Get the name of the function as a string
  func_name_str <- deparse(substitute(func_name))
  
  # Build the assignment line
  assign_statement <- paste0(func_name_str, " <- ")
  
  # Build the file path
  file_name <- file.path(folder, paste0(func_name_str, ".R"))
  
  # Get the function object itself
  function_to_export <- get(func_name_str)
  
  # Write to file
  writeLines(
    c(assign_statement, deparse(function_to_export)),
    con = file_name
  )
}

write_function(df_to_dense_flextable, folder = "Scripts")

title: 3  Overview
text:
3.1 Individual functions
The following statistics are currently catered for: mean, median and sum for numeric outcomes, percentage and count for categorical ones.
Potential additions: max, min, SD, IQR and other percentile values.
These are the functin names that calculate these.
Weighted functions:
* weighted_mean,
* weighted_median,
* weighted_sum,
* weighted_perc,
* weighted_count.
Unweighted functions:
* unweighted_mean,
* unweighted_median,
* unweighted_sum,
* unweighted_perc,
* unweighted_count.
An unweighted count is always calculated, stored in unweighted_n. When using unweighted_count it is also stored in estimate (it is duplicated).

title: 3  Overview
text:
3.1.1 Arguments
The functions above have the same arguments:

data - a dataframe for unweighted functions, a srvyr object for weighted functions. Unweighted functions will also accept srvyr objects.

outcomes - vector of otucome variable names.

predictors - list of predictor variable names. Each element is a vector and can be of length > 1 to produce nested tables.

conf - either “se” for standard errors or “ci” for confidence intervals.

base - the output of the base_information function, a sort of data dictionary of base descriptions (requires manual specification).

Data output structure:- a data frame, column names are…

cross_break - predictor variable names separated by ’ X ’. If not predictor then “Total”.

outcome - outcome variable name

o_lab - outcome variable label

o_cat - outcome variable levels, or duplicate of value in stat for numeric statistics.

predictor, p_lab and p_cat - same interpretation as for outcomes, with addition of numbers to differentiate mutliple predictors, predictor1 for the first predictor and so on.

stat - contains the statistic definition.

estimate, contains the statistics.

estimate_se for standard error.

estimate_ci present when confidence intervals calculated, but not really used at any point.
base - unweighted base size for statistics.

base_description - the output of create_bases for that row’s selection of predictor and outcome variables.

unweighted_n - cell count.

The values of stat can be:

“mean”

“median”

“sum”

“perc”
“count”

“w_mean”

“w_median”

“w_sum”

“w_perc”

“w_count”

title: 3  Overview
text:
3.2 Main supporting functions

3.2.1 Base descriptions
Consists of three functions. base_information collects a set of base descriptions linked to variable names. create_bases selects a set of those bases for a particular combination of variables used in a table, and saves them in the output in the base_description column. prepare_base_for_table then puts it in a semi-readable format for a table.


3.2.2 Multicodes
This checks to see if there is a common stem among some of the variables, which must be the case in both variable and variable labels. If there is, it reduces the variable names to that common stem and splits the variable label in two, taking the common stem to become the new variable label and placing the unique parts in the position of categories, over-writing ‘yes’. The ‘no’ responses are then filtered out. This is only done where all variables with the common stem also have the same base size. The result is an output that in the data frame appears to relate to a single variable and can afterwards be treated as one. It also includes a step to combine their base labels into a single label - really these should all be the same anyway.

title: 3  Overview
text:
3.3 A wrapper - calc_stats
Arguments, mostly the same as in the individual functions.
pval - if not NULL, then compute p-values for single predictor. No method for nested variables.
multicode - this calls a supporting function to identify and format multicode variables.
statistics - specifices which statistics to calculate. The allowed values allowed are:

“mean”

“median”

“sum”

“perc”

“count”

“w_mean”

“w_median”

“w_sum”

“w_perc”

“w_count”

Accepts multiple arguments. By default… c(“count”,“mean”).
Data output structure:- remains the same as for individual statistic functions with two additions:

p_method - the description of what significance test has been run,

p_value - a p-value, when you have a single predictor, this will be the output.

4.2.3 Function

standardise_names <- 
  function(
    data, # dataframe used to create the table in question
    out_var, # outcome variable
    preds, # Grouping predictor variables
    table # Table containing variables to be standardised 
    )    {
    
    if(any(str_detect(class(data), "survey"))){data_to_look_in <- data[["variables"]]
    } else {data_to_look_in <- data}
        
    # Create a standardised set of variable names
    standardised_variable_names <- c(paste0("p_cat", seq_along(preds)), "o_cat")

    renamed_variables <- table %>%
          # Rename df columns with standard names
          rename(any_of(setNames(c(preds,out_var), standardised_variable_names)))  %>% 
          # Add outcome variable label
          mutate(o_lab = attributes(data_to_look_in[[out_var]])$label) %>%
          # Add column with outcome variable name
          mutate(outcome = out_var) 

        # Adding predictor meta data
        all_renamed <- map(seq_len(length(preds)), function(number) {

          # for each predictor in turn - create standardised variable names
          standardised_predictor_names <- paste0(c("predictor", "p_lab"), number)

          # Extract predictor variable labels
          p_label <- attributes(data_to_look_in[[preds[number]]])$label

          # Handle missing variable labels - not been required
          if(is.null(p_label)){p_label <- preds[number]}

          # Add predictor variable names and labels to ctab
          ctab_plus_new_labels <- renamed_variables %>%
            mutate(predictor = preds[number],
                   p_lab = p_label) %>%
            # Rename predictor variables with standardised names
            rename(any_of(setNames(c("predictor", "p_lab"), standardised_predictor_names)))

          return(ctab_plus_new_labels)

           }) %>% reduce(., full_join)
    
    return(all_renamed)
        
  }

write_function(standardise_names, folder = "Scripts")

title: 4  Helper functions
text:
4.3 Base descriptions
To work with base descriptions three functions are required:

base_information - which creates a library of base descriptions for use when creating tables.
create_bases - which uses the output of base_information to know what base descriptions to put with each table.
prepare_base_for_table - takes the output of create_bases, stored within the resulting data frame, and creates a more human-readable output when formatting the resulting tables for presentation.



4.3.1 Function to create base descriptions
Purpose - creates an object you need in your environment to create tables with base sizes - it contains the variable base descriptions to use. The output is taken as an argument by functions for calculating statistics used later in the process.
Arguments.

data - the data frame containing the variables.

general_base - a character vector. A general base description for use with most variables.

specific_bases - a named character vector. Names are variable names. Content is a base description.

Where a variable has now corresponding description in specific_bases then general_base is used.

base_information <- function(
    data, 
    general_base, 
    specific_bases
) {
  
  everything_else <- general_base
  var_descriptions <- specific_bases
  
  variable_labels <- data %>% select(names(var_descriptions)) %>% var_label(unlist = T, null_action = "fill")
  all_variable_labels <- data %>% var_label(unlist = T, null_action = "fill")
  
  base_descriptions <- list(everything_else, var_descriptions, variable_labels, all_variable_labels)
  return(base_descriptions)
  
}

write_function(base_information, folder = "Scripts")


The argument to specific_bases should look like this.

var_descriptions <- rep("Self-completion questionnaire, asked of a random sub-set of respondents", 6)

4.3.2 Create base info within tables
Purpose: This is the function used within larger functions calculating statistics (mean)
create_bases takes two arguments:

base_info is the output of the base_information() function.

variables is a character vector of variable names.

It exports a character vector which contains the base description for each variable name. If base descriptions are repeated, at this point they are simply duplicated in the output vector. Where there are multiple variables, their descriptions are separated by ” X “.

create_bases <- function(
    base_info,
    variables
){
  
  # Extract the names of variables that have specific bases defined (from base_info[[2]])
  names_of_variables_with_specific_bases <- base_info[[2]] %>% names
  
  # Logical vector: TRUE if variable has a specific base and is in 'variables', FALSE otherwise
  bases_to_use <- names_of_variables_with_specific_bases %in% variables
    
  # Get the labels of the variables that match bases_to_use (from base_info[[3]])
  variable_labels_to_use <- base_info[[3]][bases_to_use]
  
  # Get the specific bases that match bases_to_use (from base_info[[2]])
  bases_to_use <- base_info[[2]][bases_to_use] 
  
  # If there are any variables with specific bases...
  if(length(bases_to_use) > 0){
    # Create base strings in the form "<base>:-  <label>"
    list_of_bases <- paste0(bases_to_use, ":-  ", variable_labels_to_use)
  } else {
    # If no specific bases apply, start with an empty vector
    list_of_bases <- c()
  }
    
  # Find variables in 'variables' that do NOT have specific bases
  variables_using_default_description <- variables[!variables %in% names_of_variables_with_specific_bases]
  
  # If there are any variables without specific bases...
  if(length(variables_using_default_description) > 0){
    # Get their labels (from base_info[[4]])
    labels_of_variables_using_default_description <- base_info[[4]][variables_using_default_description]
    
    # Create default base strings in the form "<general_base>:-  <label>"
    default_base_description <- paste0(base_info[[1]],  ":-  ", labels_of_variables_using_default_description)
    
    # Append the default descriptions to the list_of_bases
    list_of_bases <- c(list_of_bases, default_base_description)
    } 
  
  # Collapse all base strings into one single string separated by " X "
  list_of_bases <- list_of_bases %>% paste0(., collapse = " X ")
  
  return(list_of_bases) # Return the final string

}

write_function(create_bases, folder = "Scripts")

4.3.3 Create formatted bases for display under a table
Purpose: This takes the long string of base descriptions returned by create_bases and makes into a human-readable piece of text.
Why not do this all in one go, as part of create_bases? Because, this returns a description for all variables in a table, and sometimes, the output of calc_stats, the function create_bases is used within, is later broken up into sub-tables. This stage happens after that, once the final variables to be shown in a table is known.
Arguments: it has only one argument, bases_for_table, which should be the character vector returned by create_bases.
Outputs: the outputs come as a list, each element corresponding to a different base description.

prepare_base_for_table <- function(bases_for_table) {
  
  base_results <- list()  # Empty list to store results

  # Split the input string by " X " into separate base elements, then keep only unique elements
  bases <- bases_for_table %>% str_split_1(., " X ") %>% unique
  
  # From each base element, extract the part before ":-  " as base description
  base_descriptions <- bases %>% str_split_i(., ":-  ", 1)
  
  # From each base element, extract the part after ":-  " as variable label(s)
  variables <- bases %>% str_split_i(., ":-  ", 2)
  
  # Find all unique base descriptions
  unique_base_descriptions <- unique(base_descriptions)
  
  # If there is only one unique base description...
  if(length(unique_base_descriptions) == 1){
    # Append that unique base description to the results list
    base_results <- append(base_results ,list(unique_base_descriptions))
    } else {
       
  # Create a data frame of `base_descriptions` and count the occurrences of each
  most_common_base_description <- data.frame(base_descriptions = base_descriptions) %>% 
    count(base_descriptions) %>%   # Count frequency of each base description
    mutate(max_n = max(n)) %>%     # Add a column with max count value
    filter(n == max_n) %>%         # Filter to base description(s) with max count
    pull(base_descriptions) %>%    # Extract the base description(s)
    unique                         # Remove duplicates if any
  
  # If there are multiple most common base descriptions, keep only the first one
  if(length(most_common_base_description) > 1){
    most_common_base_description <- most_common_base_description[1]
    }
  
  # Format the most common base description prepended by "All other variables:- " 
  base_results[[1]] <- most_common_base_description %>% 
    paste("All other variables:- ", ., collapse = "") %>% 
    str_to_sentence() # and capitalize sentence
  
  # Remove the most common base description from the unique list to handle separately
  unique_base_descriptions <- unique_base_descriptions[!unique_base_descriptions %in% most_common_base_description]
  
  # Loop over remaining unique base descriptions
  for (xxx in unique_base_descriptions){
    
    # Find indices where the base description matches the current unique description
    index <- which(base_descriptions %in% xxx) 
    
    # Concatenate the variables associated with this base description into a comma-separated string
    # `index` identifies the relevant variable labels from `variables`
    variable_list <- paste0(variables[index], collapse = ", ") 
    
    # Create a string combining the base description and its variables
    variable_description <- paste0(xxx, ":- ", variable_list) 
    
    # Append this description to the results list
    base_results <- append(base_results, variable_description)
    
  }
  
  }

    # Most common last. 
    base_results <- rev(base_results)
    
  # Return the list of prepared base descriptions
    return(base_results)

}

4.4.1 A function for grouped median SE
Purpose: this function will be used with unweighted_median to calculate an unweighted standard error of a median within groups.

Arguments:

data - data frame in use by unweighted_median,

outcome - character vector length 1,

predictors - character vector of predictors.


grouped_medianse <- function(data, outcome, predictors){
  
  # Select only the predictor columns from the data
  data_with_required_predictors <- data %>% select(all_of(predictors)) 
  
  # For each predictor column, pull the factor vector from the data and drop unused levels
  predictors_as_list <- map(
    names(data_with_required_predictors), 
    ~data %>% pull(.x) %>% fct_drop
  )
  
  # Split the original data into subsets based on combinations of predictor factor levels
  split_data <- split(data, predictors_as_list, drop = TRUE)
  
  # For each subset of data, calculate the median standard error and create a results row
  results <- map(1:length(split_data), function(number) {
    
    # Extract the outcome variable values for the current subset
    outcome_data <- split_data[[number]] %>% pull(outcome)
    
    # Calculate the median standard error using the wrappedtools package
    median <- wrappedtools::medianse(outcome_data)
    
    # Extract the unique combination of predictor levels for this subset
    levels_in_use <- split_data[[number]] %>% 
      select(all_of(predictors)) %>% 
      unique() %>% 
      # Add a new column with the median standard error estimate
      mutate(estimate_se = median)
    
  }) %>% 
    
    bind_rows() # Combine all results into a single data frame
  
  return(results) # Return the combined data frame with predictor levels and median SE estimates
  
}

4.4.2 A function for grouped median CI
Purpose: this function willb used with unweighted_median to calculate an unweighted confidence interval around a median within groups.
Arguments:

data - data frame in use by unweighted_median,

outcome - character vector length 1,

predictors - character vector of predictors.


grouped_medianci <- function(data, outcome, predictors){
  
  # Select only the predictor columns from the data
  data_with_required_predictors <- data %>% select(all_of(predictors)) 
  
  # For each predictor column, extract its factor values from data and drop unused levels
  predictors_as_list <- map(
    names(data_with_required_predictors), 
    ~data %>% pull(.x) %>% fct_drop
  )
  
  # Split the original data frame into subsets based on the combination of factor levels in predictors_as_list
  split_data <- split(data, predictors_as_list, drop = TRUE)
  
  # For each subset in split_data...
  results <- map(1:length(split_data), function(number) {
    
    # Pull the outcome variable values for this subset
    outcome_data <- split_data[[number]] %>% pull(outcome)
    
    # Proceed only if there are more than 5 observations in the subset
    if(length(outcome_data) > 5){
      
      # Calculate median confidence interval with bootstrap (from wrappedtools package)
      cil <- wrappedtools::median_cl_boot(outcome_data)
      
      # Extract the unique combination of predictor levels for this subset
      levels_in_use <- split_data[[number]] %>% 
        select(all_of(predictors)) %>% 
        unique() %>% 
        # Add the lower and upper confidence interval bounds as new columns
        mutate(estimate_low = cil$CIlow, estimate_upp = cil$CIhigh)
      
      # Return this data frame with predictor levels and confidence intervals
      return(levels_in_use) 
    }
  }) %>% 
    # Combine the list of data frames into one data frame
    bind_rows()
  
  # Return the combined results
  return(results)
  
}

4.5 Significance testing
Data filtered on both outcome and predictor variables.
Predictor already a factor. Outcome either already numeric or a factor.

* “sum”

4.5.1 Numeric variables, unweighted

# df2
# data <- df3
# outcome <- "skipmeal2"
# predictor <- "RSex"

unweighted_test_numeric_by_cat <- function(data, outcome, predictor) {
  
  x <- data %>% pull(predictor)
  y <- data %>% pull(outcome)
  
  x_lab <- data %>% select(all_of(predictor)) %>% var_label(unlist = TRUE, null_action = "fill")
  y_lab <- data %>% select(all_of(outcome)) %>% var_label(unlist = TRUE, null_action = "fill")

  # Remove missing values
  complete_idx <- complete.cases(y, x)
  y <- y[complete_idx]
  x <- x[complete_idx]
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    # Check normality of residuals (Shapiro-Wilk)
    model <- lm(y ~ x)
    shapiro_p <- shapiro.test(residuals(model))$p.value
    
    # Decision
    if (shapiro_p < 0.05) {
      # Non-normal → Kruskal–Wallis
      method_used <- "Kruskal–Wallis"
      p_val <- kruskal.test(y ~ x)$p.value
    } else {
      # Normal enough → Welch's ANOVA
      method_used <- "Welch's ANOVA"
      p_val <- oneway.test(y ~ x, var.equal = FALSE)$p.value
    }
    
    list(method = method_used, p = p_val)
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    list(method = "Significance test returned an error.", p = NA)
  })
  
  result <- tibble(
    cross_break = predictor,
    predictor1 = predictor, 
    p_lab1 = x_lab, 
    outcome = outcome, 
    o_lab = y_lab,
    p_method = result$method,
    p_value = result$p
  )
  
  result <- map_df(c("mean", "median", "sum"), ~result %>% mutate(stat = .x))  
  
  return(result)
  
}

# data <- df_svy
# outcome <- "welfare2"
# predictor <- "RSex"

weighted_test_numeric_by_cat <- function(data, outcome, predictor) {
  
  suppressMessages({
  
  x_lab <- data[["variables"]] %>% select(all_of(predictor)) %>% var_label(unlist = TRUE, null_action = "fill")
  y_lab <- data[["variables"]] %>% select(all_of(outcome)) %>% var_label(unlist = TRUE, null_action = "fill")

  # Remove missing values
  filtered_data <- data %>% filter(if_all(c(outcome, predictor), ~!is.na(.x)))
  frmla <- paste0(outcome, " ~ ", predictor)
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    # Check normality of residuals (Shapiro-Wilk)
    model <- survey::svyglm(frmla, design = filtered_data)
    shapiro_p <- shapiro.test(residuals(model))$p.value
    
    # Decision
    if (shapiro_p < 0.05) {
      # Non-normal → Kruskal–Wallis
      method_used <- "Kruskal–Wallis"
      p_val <- survey::svyranktest(frmla, design = filtered_data)$p.value
    } else {
      # Normal enough → Welch's ANOVA
      method_used <- "Wald Test"
      anova_result <- survey::regTermTest(model, predictor)
      p_val <- anova_result[["p"]] %>% as.vector()
    }
    
    list(method = method_used, p = p_val)
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    list(method = "Significance test returned an error.", p = NA)
  })
  
  result <- tibble(
      cross_break = predictor,
      predictor1 = predictor, 
      p_lab1 = x_lab, 
      outcome = outcome, 
      o_lab = y_lab,
      p_method = result$method,
      p_value = result$p
    )
  
  result <- map_df(c("w_mean", "w_median", "w_sum"), ~result %>% mutate(stat = .x))  
  
  return(result)
  
  })
}

unweighted_test_cat_by_cat <- function(data, outcome, predictor) {
  
  x <- data %>% pull(predictor)
  y <- data %>% pull(outcome)
  
  x_lab <- data %>% select(all_of(predictor)) %>% var_label(unlist = TRUE, null_action = "fill")
  y_lab <- data %>% select(all_of(outcome)) %>% var_label(unlist = TRUE, null_action = "fill")

  # Remove missing values
  complete_idx <- complete.cases(y, x)
  y <- y[complete_idx]
  x <- x[complete_idx]
  
  result <- tryCatch({

      # chi-square test
      method_used <- "Chi-Square test"
      p_val <- chisq.test(x, y)$p.value
    
    list(method = method_used, p = p_val)
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    list(method = "Significance test returned an error.", p = NA)
  })
  
  result <- tibble(
      cross_break = predictor,
      predictor1 = predictor, 
      p_lab1 = x_lab, 
      outcome = outcome, 
      o_lab = y_lab,
      p_method = result$method,
      p_value = result$p
     )

  result <- map_df(c("perc", "count"), ~result %>% mutate(stat = .x))  
  
  return(result)

}

weighted_test_cat_by_cat <- function(data, outcome, predictor) {
  
  x_lab <- data[["variables"]] %>% select(all_of(predictor)) %>% var_label(unlist = TRUE, null_action = "fill")
  y_lab <- data[["variables"]] %>% select(all_of(outcome)) %>% var_label(unlist = TRUE, null_action = "fill")

  # Remove missing values
  filtered_data <- data %>% filter(if_all(c(outcome, predictor), ~!is.na(.x)))
  frmla <- formula(paste0("~",outcome,  " + " , predictor))
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    
      # chi-square test
      method_used <- "Chi-Square test"
      p_val <- svychisq(frmla, design = filtered_data, statistic = "adjWald")$p.value
      p_val <- p_val %>% as.vector()
      
    list(method = method_used, p = p_val)
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    list(method = "Significance test returned an error.", p = NA)
  })
  
  result <- tibble(
    cross_break = predictor,
    predictor1 = predictor, 
    p_lab1 = x_lab, 
    outcome = outcome, 
    o_lab = y_lab,
    p_method = result$method,
    p_value = result$p
  )

  result <- map_df(c("w_perc", "w_count"), ~result %>% mutate(stat = .x))  
  
  return(result)
  
}

4.6 p.values wrapper

return_pvalues <- function(data, outcome, predictor){

    if(any(str_detect(class(data), "survey"))){
      data_2 <- data[["variables"]]
      weights <- "weights"
    } else {
        data_2 <- data
        weights <- "no weights"
    }
  
  outcome_class_factor <- class(data_2 %>% pull(outcome)) %>% str_detect(., "factor") %>% any()
  
  if(weights == "no weights"){
    
    if(outcome_class_factor == TRUE){
      result <- unweighted_test_cat_by_cat(data = data, outcome = outcome, predictor = predictor)
    } else { 
      result <- unweighted_test_numeric_by_cat(data = data, outcome = outcome, predictor = predictor)
    }
    
  } else {
    
    if(outcome_class_factor == TRUE){
      result <- weighted_test_cat_by_cat(data = data, outcome = outcome, predictor = predictor) 
    } else { 
      result <- weighted_test_numeric_by_cat(data = data, outcome = outcome, predictor = predictor)
    }
    
  }
  
  return(result)

}

5.2.1 unweighted_mean

unweighted_mean <- function(
    data, # a data frame
    outcomes, # a character vector of outcome variables
    predictors = NULL, # a list, each element containing a character vector of predictor variables
    conf = NULL, # "se" or "ci"; returns either standard error or confidence intervals 
    base = NULL
) {suppressMessages({suppressWarnings({
  
  output <- map(outcomes, function(cur_outcome) {
    
    base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = cur_outcome)) 
        
    # Remove missing data
    one_total_table <- data %>% 
      filter(!is.na(.data[[cur_outcome]])) %>% 
      summarise(estimate = mean(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T), 
          n = n(), 
          sd = sd(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T), 
          estimate_se = sd / sqrt(n), 
          estimate_low = estimate - 1.96 * estimate_se,
          estimate_upp = estimate + 1.96 * estimate_se, 
          base = sum(n)) %>% 
          select(-n, -sd) %>% 
        mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "mean") %>% 
        mutate(outcome = cur_outcome) %>% 
        rename(any_of(c(o_cat = cur_outcome))) %>% 
        mutate(o_lab = attributes(data[[cur_outcome]])$label) %>% 
        mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
  
    # Create cross-breaks
    if(!is.null(predictors)){
    predictor_tables <- map(predictors, function(cur_predictor) { 
      
            # Handle cases with and without predictor variables
        if (length(cur_predictor) > 0) {
          
          # Vector containing predictors and outcomes
          predictor_and_outcome <- c(cur_predictor, cur_outcome)
          base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = predictor_and_outcome)) 
          
          one_predictor_table <- data %>%
            # Filter missing values
            filter(rowSums(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome), ~ is.na(.))) == 0) %>%
            # Group data
            group_by(across(all_of(cur_predictor))) %>% 
            # Weighted mean + base sizes, with grouping vars
            summarise(estimate = mean(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T), 
                      n = n(), 
                      sd = sd(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T), 
                      estimate_se = sd / sqrt(n), 
                      estimate_low = estimate - 1.96 * estimate_se,
                      estimate_upp = estimate + 1.96 * estimate_se, 
                      base = sum(n)) %>% 
                      select(-n, -sd) %>% 
            # Added for consistency when merged with categorical outcome tables. 
            mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "mean") %>% 
            # Standardise names so can stack results across different predictors and outcomes. 
            standardise_names(data = data, preds = cur_predictor, out_var = cur_outcome) %>%
            mutate(cross_break = paste0(cur_predictor, collapse = "_X_")) %>%
            mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
        }
      
      return(one_predictor_table)
      
    })
    
    # Stack tables one on another
    predictor_tables <- bind_rows(predictor_tables)
    
    } # Predictors ends
    
    # Bind crossbreaks and frequency table together
    if(!is.null(predictors)){table_for_one_outcome <- bind_rows(one_total_table, predictor_tables)
    } else {table_for_one_outcome <- one_total_table}
    
    table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>%
      mutate(stat = "mean") %>%
      # Add 'Total' to predictor category variables for frequency section of the table.
      mutate(across(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), ~case_when(is.na(.x) ~ "Total", TRUE ~ as.character(.x)))) %>%
      # Reorder variables
      select(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), outcome, o_lab, o_cat, stat, contains("estimate"), base, base_description) 
  
    if(!is.null(conf)){
      if(conf == "ci"){
        table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% 
          mutate(estimate_ci = paste0(as.character(estimate_low), " - ", as.character(estimate_upp)))}
    } else { 
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-", .after = estimate) %>% 
        select(-estimate_low, -estimate_upp)
    }
    
    return(table_for_one_outcome)
    
  }) # Outcomes loop ends 
  
  # Stack tables one on another
  output <- output %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(unweighted_n = base)
  
  # Either drop standard errors or confidence intervals
  if(!is.null(conf)){
  if(conf == "se"){keep <- c("upp", "low")} else {keep <- "_se"}
    output <- output %>% select(!ends_with(keep))
  }
  
  return(output)
  
})})
}

5.2.2 unweighted_median

unweighted_median <- function(
    data, # a data frame
    outcomes, # a character vector of outcome variables
    predictors = NULL, # a list, each element containing a character vector of predictor variables
    conf = NULL, # "se" or "ci"; returns either standard error or confidence intervals 
    base = NULL
) {suppressMessages({suppressWarnings({
  
  output <- map(outcomes, function(cur_outcome) {
    
    base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = cur_outcome)) 
        
    # Remove missing data
    one_total_table <- data %>% 
      filter(!is.na(.data[[cur_outcome]])) %>% 
      summarise(estimate = median(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T),
                base = n())
      
    if(!is.null(conf)){
      if(conf == "se"){
      median_se <- wrappedtools::medianse(data %>% pull(cur_outcome))
      one_total_table <- one_total_table %>% mutate(estimate_se = median_se)
      } else {
      median_ci <- wrappedtools::median_cl_boot(data %>% pull(cur_outcome))
      one_total_table <- one_total_table %>% mutate(
        estimate_low = median_ci$CIlow,
        estimate_upp = median_ci$CIhigh)
      }
    } else {
      one_total_table <- one_total_table %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-")
    }
    
     one_total_table <- one_total_table %>% 
        mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "median") %>% 
        mutate(outcome = cur_outcome) %>% 
        rename(any_of(c(o_cat = cur_outcome))) %>% 
        mutate(o_lab = attributes(data[[cur_outcome]])$label) %>% 
        mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
  
    # Create cross-breaks
    if(!is.null(predictors)){
    predictor_tables <- map(predictors, function(cur_predictor) { 
      
            # Handle cases with and without predictor variables
        if (length(cur_predictor) > 0) {
          
          # Vector containing predictors and outcomes
          predictor_and_outcome <- c(cur_predictor, cur_outcome)
          base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = predictor_and_outcome)) # edit

          one_predictor_table <- data %>%
            # Filter missing values
            filter(rowSums(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome), ~ is.na(.))) == 0) %>%
            # Group data
            group_by(across(all_of(cur_predictor))) %>% 
            # Weighted mean + base sizes, with grouping vars
            summarise(estimate = median(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T),
                base = n())
          
      if(!is.null(conf)){
         if(conf == "se"){
           median_se <- grouped_medianse(data = data, predictors = cur_predictor, outcome = cur_outcome)
           one_predictor_table <- one_predictor_table %>% full_join(median_se)
          }
          else {
            median_ci <- grouped_medianci(data = data, predictors = cur_predictor, outcome = cur_outcome)
            one_predictor_table <- one_predictor_table %>% full_join(median_ci)
          }
      } else {
      one_predictor_table <- one_predictor_table %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-")
      }
      
          # Added for consistency when merged with categorical outcome tables. 
          one_predictor_table <- one_predictor_table %>% mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "median") %>% 
            # Standardise names so can stack results across different predictors and outcomes. 
            standardise_names(data = data, preds = cur_predictor, out_var = cur_outcome) %>%
            mutate(cross_break = paste0(cur_predictor, collapse = "_X_"))  %>%
            mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
            
        }
      
      
      return(one_predictor_table)
      
    })
    
    # Stack tables one on another
    predictor_tables <- bind_rows(predictor_tables)
    
    } # Predictors ends
    
    # Bind crossbreaks and frequency table together
    if(!is.null(predictors)){table_for_one_outcome <- bind_rows(one_total_table, predictor_tables)
    } else {table_for_one_outcome <- one_total_table}
    
    table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>%
      mutate(stat = "median") %>%
      # Add 'Total' to predictor category variables for frequency section of the table.
      mutate(across(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), ~case_when(is.na(.x) ~ "Total", TRUE ~ as.character(.x)))) %>%
      # Reorder variables
      select(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), outcome, o_lab, o_cat, stat, contains("estimate"), base, base_description) 
    
    if(!is.null(conf)){
    if(conf == "ci"){
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% 
        mutate(estimate_ci = paste0(as.character(estimate_low), " - ", as.character(estimate_upp)))
    }
    }
    
    return(table_for_one_outcome)
    
  }) # Outcomes loop ends 
  
  # Stack tables one on another
  output <- output %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(unweighted_n = base)
  
  # Either drop standard errors or confidence intervals
  if(!is.null(conf)){
  if(conf == "se"){keep <- c("upp", "low")} else {keep <- "_se"}
    output <- output %>% select(!ends_with(keep))
  }
  
  return(output)
  
})})
}

5.2.3 unweighted_sum

unweighted_sum <- function(
    data, # a data frame
    outcomes, # a character vector of outcome variables
    predictors = NULL, # a list, each element containing a character vector of predictor variables
    conf = NULL, # "se" or "ci"; returns either standard error or confidence intervals 
    base = NULL
) {suppressMessages({suppressWarnings({
  
  output <- map(outcomes, function(cur_outcome) {
    
    base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = cur_outcome)) 

    # Remove missing data
    one_total_table <- data %>% 
      filter(!is.na(.data[[cur_outcome]])) %>% 
      summarise(estimate = sum(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T), 
            base = n(), 
            sd = sd(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T), 
            estimate_se = sd * sqrt(base), 
            estimate_low = estimate - 1.96 * estimate_se,
            estimate_upp = estimate + 1.96 * estimate_se
            ) %>% select(-sd)
    
     one_total_table <- one_total_table %>% 
        mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "sum") %>% 
        mutate(outcome = cur_outcome) %>% 
        rename(any_of(c(o_cat = cur_outcome))) %>% 
        mutate(o_lab = attributes(data[[cur_outcome]])$label) %>% 
        mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
  
    # Create cross-breaks
    if(!is.null(predictors)){
    predictor_tables <- map(predictors, function(cur_predictor) { 
      
            # Handle cases with and without predictor variables
        if (length(cur_predictor) > 0) {
          
          # Vector containing predictors and outcomes
          predictor_and_outcome <- c(cur_predictor, cur_outcome)
          base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = predictor_and_outcome)) 
          
          one_predictor_table <- data %>%
            # Filter missing values
            filter(rowSums(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome), ~ is.na(.))) == 0) %>%
            # Group data
            group_by(across(all_of(cur_predictor))) %>% 
            # Weighted mean + base sizes, with grouping vars
            summarise(estimate = sum(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T), 
            base = n(), 
            sd = sd(!!sym(cur_outcome), na.rm = T), 
            estimate_se = sd * sqrt(base), 
            estimate_low = estimate - 1.96 * estimate_se,
            estimate_upp = estimate + 1.96 * estimate_se
            ) %>% select(-sd)
      
          # Added for consistency when merged with categorical outcome tables. 
          one_predictor_table <- one_predictor_table %>% mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "sum") %>% 
            # Standardise names so can stack results across different predictors and outcomes. 
            standardise_names(data = data, preds = cur_predictor, out_var = cur_outcome) %>%
            mutate(cross_break = paste0(cur_predictor, collapse = "_X_")) %>%
            mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
            
        }
      
      return(one_predictor_table)
      
    })
    
    # Stack tables one on another
    predictor_tables <- bind_rows(predictor_tables)
    
    } # Predictors ends
    
    # Bind crossbreaks and frequency table together
    if(!is.null(predictors)){table_for_one_outcome <- bind_rows(one_total_table, predictor_tables)
    } else {table_for_one_outcome <- one_total_table}
    
    table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>%
      mutate(stat = "sum") %>% 
      # Add 'Total' to predictor category variables for frequency section of the table.
      mutate(across(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), ~case_when(is.na(.x) ~ "Total", TRUE ~ as.character(.x)))) %>%
      # Reorder variables
      select(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), outcome, o_lab, o_cat, stat, contains("estimate"), base, base_description) 
    
    if(!is.null(conf)){
      if(conf == "ci"){
        table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% 
          mutate(estimate_ci = paste0(as.character(estimate_low), " - ", as.character(estimate_upp)))
      }
    } else {
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-") %>% 
        select(-estimate_upp, -estimate_low)
    }
    
    return(table_for_one_outcome)
    
  }) # Outcomes loop ends 
  
  # Stack tables one on another
  output <- output %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(unweighted_n = base)
  
  # Either drop standard errors or confidence intervals
  if(!is.null(conf)){
  if(conf == "se"){keep <- c("upp", "low")} else {keep <- "_se"}
    output <- output %>% select(!ends_with(keep))
  }
  
  return(output)
  
})})
}

            mutate(estimate = unweighted_n / sum(unweighted_n, na.rm = T), 
               estimate_se = sqrt(estimate * (1 - estimate) / sum(unweighted_n)), 
               estimate_low = (estimate - 1.96 * estimate_se),
               estimate_upp = (estimate + 1.96 * estimate_se),
               base = sum(unweighted_n, na.rm = T)
             )
      
          # Added for consistency when merged with categorical outcome tables. 
          one_predictor_table <- one_predictor_table %>% 
            # Standardise names so can stack results across different predictors and outcomes. 
            standardise_names(data = data, preds = cur_predictor, out_var = cur_outcome) %>%
            mutate(cross_break = paste0(cur_predictor, collapse = "_X_")) %>%
            mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
            
        }
      
      return(one_predictor_table)
      
    })
    
    # Stack tables one on another
    predictor_tables <- bind_rows(predictor_tables)
    
    } # Predictors ends
    
    # Bind crossbreaks and frequency table together
    if(!is.null(predictors)){table_for_one_outcome <- bind_rows(one_total_table, predictor_tables)
    } else {table_for_one_outcome <- one_total_table}
    
    table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>%
      mutate(stat = "perc") %>%
      # Add 'Total' to predictor category variables for frequency section of the table.
      mutate(across(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), ~case_when(is.na(.x) ~ "Total", TRUE ~ as.character(.x)))) %>%
      # Reorder variables
      select(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), outcome, o_lab, o_cat, stat, contains("estimate"), unweighted_n, base, base_description) 
    
    if(!is.null(conf)){
      if(conf == "ci"){
        table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% 
          mutate(estimate_ci = paste0(as.character(estimate_low), " - ", as.character(estimate_upp)))
      }
    } else {
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-") %>% 
        select(-estimate_upp, -estimate_low)
    }
    

    return(table_for_one_outcome)
    
  }) # Outcomes loop ends 
  
  # Stack tables one on another
  output <- output %>% bind_rows()
  
  # Either drop standard errors or confidence intervals
  if(!is.null(conf)){
  if(conf == "se"){keep <- c("upp", "low")} else {keep <- "_se"}
    output <- output %>% select(!ends_with(keep))
  }
  
  return(output)
  
})})
}

5.2.5 unweighted_count

unweighted_count <- function(
    data, # a data frame
    outcomes, # a character vector of outcome variables
    predictors = NULL, # a list, each element containing a character vector of predictor variables
    conf = NULL, # "se" or "ci"; returns either standard error or confidence intervals 
    base = NULL
) {suppressMessages({suppressWarnings({
  
  output <- map(outcomes, function(cur_outcome) {
    
    base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = cur_outcome)) # edit

    # Remove missing data
    one_total_table <- data %>% 
      filter(!is.na(.data[[cur_outcome]])) %>% 
      count(.data[[cur_outcome]], name = "estimate") %>%    
      mutate(base = sum(estimate, na.rm = T), 
             prop = estimate / base,
             estimate_se = sqrt(base * prop * (1 - prop)),
             estimate_low = (estimate - 1.96 * estimate_se),
             estimate_upp = (estimate + 1.96 * estimate_se),
             ) %>% 
      select(-prop) %>% 
      mutate(outcome = cur_outcome) %>% 
      rename(any_of(c(o_cat = cur_outcome))) %>% 
      mutate(o_lab = attributes(data[[cur_outcome]])$label) %>% 
      mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
  
    # Create cross-breaks
    if(!is.null(predictors)){
    predictor_tables <- map(predictors, function(cur_predictor) { 
      
            # Handle cases with and without predictor variables
        if (length(cur_predictor) > 0) {
          
          # Vector containing predictors and outcomes
          predictor_and_outcome <- c(cur_predictor, cur_outcome)
          base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = predictor_and_outcome)) 
          
          one_predictor_table <- data %>%
            # Filter missing values
            filter(rowSums(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome), ~ is.na(.))) == 0) %>%
            # Group data
            group_by(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome))) %>% 
            summarise(estimate = n()) %>%
            group_by(across(all_of(cur_predictor))) %>% 
            mutate(
              base = sum(estimate, na.rm = T),
              prop = estimate / sum(base), 
              estimate_se = sqrt(base * prop * (1 - prop)),
              estimate_low = (estimate - 1.96 * estimate_se),
              estimate_upp = (estimate + 1.96 * estimate_se)
             ) %>% select(-prop)
      
          # Added for consistency when merged with categorical outcome tables. 
          one_predictor_table <- one_predictor_table %>% 
            # Standardise names so can stack results across different predictors and outcomes. 
            standardise_names(data = data, preds = cur_predictor, out_var = cur_outcome) %>%
            mutate(cross_break = paste0(cur_predictor, collapse = "_X_")) %>%
            mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
            
        }
      
      return(one_predictor_table)
      
    })
    
    # Stack tables one on another
    predictor_tables <- bind_rows(predictor_tables)
    
    } # Predictors ends
    
    # Bind crossbreaks and frequency table together
    if(!is.null(predictors)){table_for_one_outcome <- bind_rows(one_total_table, predictor_tables)
    } else {table_for_one_outcome <- one_total_table}
    
    table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>%
      mutate(stat = "count", unweighted_n = estimate) %>%
      # Add 'Total' to predictor category variables for frequency section of the table.
      mutate(across(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), ~case_when(is.na(.x) ~ "Total", TRUE ~ as.character(.x)))) %>%
      # Reorder variables
      select(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), outcome, o_lab, o_cat, stat, contains("estimate"), unweighted_n, base, base_description) 
    
    if(!is.null(conf)){
      if(conf == "ci"){
        table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% 
          mutate(estimate_ci = paste0(as.character(estimate_low), " - ", as.character(estimate_upp)))
      }
    } else {
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-") %>% 
        select(-estimate_upp, -estimate_low)
    }
    
    

    return(table_for_one_outcome)
    
  }) # Outcomes loop ends 
  
  # Stack tables one on another
  output <- output %>% bind_rows()
  
  # Either drop standard errors or confidence intervals
  if(!is.null(conf)){
  if(conf == "se"){keep <- c("upp", "low")} else {keep <- "_se"}
    output <- output %>% select(!ends_with(keep))
  }
  
  return(output)
  
})})
}

title: 6  Weighted statistics
text:
6.2 Weighted functions

Numeric variables - weighted_mean.

Numeric variables - weighted_median.

Numeric variables - weighted_sum.

Categorical variables - weighted_perc.

Categorical variables - weighted_count.


6.2.1 Weighted means

weighted_mean <- function(
    data, # a srvyr design object
    outcomes, # a character vector of outcome variables
    predictors = NULL, # a list, each element containing a character vector of predictor variables
    conf = NULL, # "se" or "ci"; returns either standard error or confidence intervals
    base = NULL
) {suppressMessages({suppressWarnings({
  
  output <- map(outcomes, function(cur_outcome) {
    
    base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = cur_outcome)) # edit
    
    # Remove missing data
    one_total_table <- data %>% 
      filter(!is.na(.data[[cur_outcome]])) %>% 
      summarise(estimate = survey_mean(!!sym(cur_outcome), vartype = conf), 
                base = unweighted(n())) %>% 
        mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "w_mean") %>% 
        mutate(outcome = cur_outcome) %>% 
        rename(any_of(c(o_cat = cur_outcome))) %>% 
        mutate(o_lab = attributes(data$variables[[cur_outcome]])$label) %>% 
      # edit
      mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 

    # Create cross-breaks
    if(!is.null(predictors)){
    predictor_tables <- map(predictors, function(cur_predictor) { 
      
            # Handle cases with and without predictor variables
        if (length(cur_predictor) > 0) {
          
          # Vector containing predictors and outcomes
          predictor_and_outcome <- c(cur_predictor, cur_outcome)
          base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = predictor_and_outcome)) # edit
          
          one_predictor_table <- data %>%
            # Filter missing values
            filter(rowSums(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome), ~ is.na(.))) == 0) %>%
            # Group data
            group_by(across(all_of(cur_predictor))) %>% 
            # Weighted mean + base sizes, with grouping vars
            summarise(estimate = survey_mean(!!sym(cur_outcome), vartype = conf), 
                      base = unweighted(n())) %>% 
            # Added for consistency when merged with categorical outcome tables. 
            mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "w_mean") %>% 
            # Standardise names so can stack results across different predictors and outcomes. 
            standardise_names(data = data, preds = cur_predictor, out_var = cur_outcome) %>%
            mutate(cross_break = paste0(cur_predictor, collapse = "_X_")) %>%
            # edit
            mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
        
        }
      
      return(one_predictor_table)
      
    })
    
    predictor_tables <- bind_rows(predictor_tables)
    
    } # Predictors ends
    
    # Bind crossbreaks and frequency table together
    if(!is.null(predictors)){table_for_one_outcome <- bind_rows(one_total_table, predictor_tables)
    } else {table_for_one_outcome <- one_total_table}
    
    table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>%
      # Record statistic calculated
      mutate(stat = "w_mean") %>%
      # Add 'Total' to predictor category variables for frequency section of the table.
      mutate(across(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), ~case_when(is.na(.x) ~ "Total", TRUE ~ .x))) %>%
      # Reorder variables
      select(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), outcome, o_lab, o_cat, stat, contains("estimate"), base, base_description) # edit
    
    if(!is.null(conf)){
    if(conf == "ci"){
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% 
        mutate(estimate_ci = paste0(as.character(estimate_low), " - ", as.character(estimate_upp)))}
    } else { 
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-", .after = estimate)
      }

    return(table_for_one_outcome)
    
  }) # Outcomes loop ends 
  
  output <- output %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(unweighted_n = base)
  
  return(output)
  
})})
}

title: 6  Weighted statistics
text:
6.3 Weighted medians

weighted_median <- function(
    data, # a srvyr design object
    outcomes, # a character vector of outcome variables
    predictors = NULL, # a list, each element containing a character vector of predictor variables
    conf = NULL, # "se" or "ci"; returns either standard error or confidence intervals 
    base = NULL
) {suppressMessages({suppressWarnings({
  
  output <- map(outcomes, function(cur_outcome) {
    # Remove missing data
    base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = cur_outcome)) # edit

    one_total_table <- data %>% 
      filter(!is.na(.data[[cur_outcome]])) %>% 
      summarise(estimate = survey_median(!!sym(zap_labels(cur_outcome)), vartype = conf), 
                base = unweighted(n())) %>% 
        mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "w_median") %>% 
        mutate(outcome = cur_outcome) %>% 
        rename(any_of(c(o_cat = cur_outcome))) %>% 
        mutate(o_lab = attributes(data$variables[[cur_outcome]])$label) %>% 
      mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
  
    # Create cross-breaks
    if(!is.null(predictors)){
    predictor_tables <- map(predictors, function(cur_predictor) { 
      
            # Handle cases with and without predictor variables
        if (length(cur_predictor) > 0) {
          
          # Vector containing predictors and outcomes
          predictor_and_outcome <- c(cur_predictor, cur_outcome)
          base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = predictor_and_outcome))
          
          one_predictor_table <- data %>%
            # Filter missing values
            filter(rowSums(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome), ~ is.na(.))) == 0) %>%
            # Group data
            group_by(across(all_of(cur_predictor))) %>% 
            # Weighted median + base sizes, with grouping vars
            summarise(estimate = survey_median(!!sym(zap_labels(cur_outcome)), vartype = conf),
                      base = unweighted(n())) %>% 
            # Added for consistency when merged with categorical outcome tables. 
            mutate("{cur_outcome}" := "w_median") %>% 
            # Standardise names so can stack results across different predictors and outcomes. 
            standardise_names(data = data, preds = cur_predictor, out_var = cur_outcome) %>%
            mutate(cross_break = paste0(cur_predictor, collapse = "_X_")) %>%
            mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
        }
      
      return(one_predictor_table)
      
    })
    
    predictor_tables <- bind_rows(predictor_tables)
    
    } # Predictors ends
    
    # Bind crossbreaks and frequency table together
    if(!is.null(predictors)){table_for_one_outcome <- bind_rows(one_total_table, predictor_tables)
    } else {table_for_one_outcome <- one_total_table}
    
    table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>%
      # Record statistic calculated
      mutate(stat = "w_median") %>%
      # Add 'Total' to predictor category variables for frequency section of the table.
      mutate(across(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), ~case_when(is.na(.x) ~ "Total", TRUE ~ .x))) %>%
      # Reorder variables
      select(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), outcome, o_lab, o_cat, stat, contains("estimate"), base, base_description) 
    
    if(!is.null(conf)){
      if(conf == "ci"){
        table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% 
          mutate(estimate_ci = paste0(as.character(estimate_low), " - ", as.character(estimate_upp)))}
    } else { 
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-", .after = estimate)
    }

    return(table_for_one_outcome)
    
  }) # Outcomes loop ends 
  
  output <- output %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(unweighted_n = base)
  
  return(output)
  
})})
}

title: 6  Weighted statistics
text:
6.5 Weighted percentages

weighted_perc <- function(
    data, # a srvyr design object
    outcomes, # a character vector of outcome variables
    predictors = NULL, # a list, each element containing a character vector of predictor variables
    conf = NULL, # "se" or "ci"; returns either standard error or confidence intervals 
    base = NULL
) {suppressMessages({suppressWarnings({
  
  output <- map(outcomes, function(cur_outcome) {
    
    base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = cur_outcome)) # edit
    
    # Remove missing data
    one_total_table <- data %>% 
      filter(!is.na(.data[[cur_outcome]])) %>% 
      group_by(across(all_of(cur_outcome))) %>% 
      summarise(estimate = survey_prop(vartype = conf), 
                unweighted_n = unweighted(n())) %>% 
      mutate(base = sum(unweighted_n, na.rm = T)) %>%
      mutate(outcome = cur_outcome) %>% 
      rename(any_of(c(o_cat = cur_outcome))) %>% 
      mutate(o_lab = attributes(data$variables[[cur_outcome]])$label) %>% 
      mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
  
    # Create cross-breaks
    if(!is.null(predictors)){
    predictor_tables <- map(predictors, function(cur_predictor) { 
  
            # Handle cases with and without predictor variables
        if (length(cur_predictor) > 0) {
          
          # Vector containing predictors and outcomes
          predictor_and_outcome <- c(cur_predictor, cur_outcome)
          base_defintion <- ifelse(is.null(base), NA, create_bases(base_info = base, variables = predictor_and_outcome)) # edit
          
          one_predictor_table <- data %>%
            # Filter missing values
            filter(rowSums(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome), ~ is.na(.))) == 0) %>%
            # Group data
            group_by(across(all_of(predictor_and_outcome))) %>% 
            # Weighted percentage + base sizes, with grouping vars
            summarise(estimate = survey_prop(vartype = conf), 
                      unweighted_n = unweighted(n())) %>% 
            mutate(base = sum(unweighted_n, na.rm = T)) %>%
            # Standardise names so can stack results across different predictors and outcomes. 
            standardise_names(data = data, preds = cur_predictor, out_var = cur_outcome) %>%
            mutate(cross_break = paste0(cur_predictor, collapse = "_X_")) %>%
            mutate(base_description = base_defintion) # descriptor label for base 
        }
      
      return(one_predictor_table)
      
    })
    
    predictor_tables <- bind_rows(predictor_tables)
    
    } # Predictors ends
    
    # Bind crossbreaks and frequency table together
    if(!is.null(predictors)){table_for_one_outcome <- bind_rows(one_total_table, predictor_tables)
    } else {table_for_one_outcome <- one_total_table}
    
    table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>%
      mutate(stat = "w_perc") %>%
      # Add 'Total' to predictor category variables for frequency section of the table.
      mutate(across(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), ~case_when(is.na(.x) ~ "Total", TRUE ~ .x))) %>%
      # Reorder variables
      select(contains(c("cross_break", "predictor", "p_lab", "p_cat")), outcome, o_lab, o_cat, stat, contains("estimate"), base, base_description, unweighted_n) 
    
    if(!is.null(conf)){
      if(conf == "ci"){
        table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% 
          mutate(estimate_ci = paste0(as.character(estimate_low), " - ", as.character(estimate_upp)))}
    } else { 
      table_for_one_outcome <- table_for_one_outcome %>% mutate(estimate_se = "-", .after = estimate)
    }

    return(table_for_one_outcome)
    
  }) # Outcomes loop ends 
  
  output <- output %>% bind_rows() %>% mutate(unweighted_n = base)
  
  return(output)
  
})})
}

This function then returns list depth. If depth equals 1 then use same predictors for all outcomes. If depth equals 2 then try and use different sets of predictors for different outcomes.

list_depth <- function(x) {
  if (!is.list(x)) {
    return(0)  # Not a list → depth 0
  } else if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(1)  # Empty list → depth 1
  } else {
    return(1 + max(sapply(x, list_depth)))
  }
}

write_function(list_depth, folder = "Scripts")

list_depth(nested_predictors)

[1] 2

# Returns TRUE if all variables in list appear in data
# Otherwise returns FALSE
vars_exist <- function(variable_list, data){
  
  if(any(grepl("survey", class(data)))){
    df_to_check <- data[["variables"]]
    } else {
      df_to_check <- data
      }
  
  predictors <- variable_list %>% unlist %>% unique
  variables_in_df <- names(df_to_check)
  
  variables_in_both <- intersect(predictors, variables_in_df)
  
  length(predictors) == length(variables_in_both)

  }

check_all_factors <- function(data, variable_list){

  if(any(grepl("survey", class(data)))){
    df_to_check <- data[["variables"]]
    } else {
      df_to_check <- data
      }
  
  df_to_check %>% select(all_of(unlist(variable_list))) %>%
    map_chr(., ~paste0(class(.x), collapse = ", ")) %>% 
    unique == "factor"
}

title: 8  Multicodes
text:
8.2 Identify Multicodes

8.2.1 Steps overview
This code identifies variables with: a) a stem divider, I will use “:”, b) a matching set of values on the left hand side of the stem divider, c) No more than 2 unique values in its levels, and d) the same base size.
So, the variable labels will be split in two around “:”. A multicode set is one where all the left hand sides of the resulting variable are the same.
But how to identify matching sets?
Once done it will replace variable label with the left hand part of the stem.
The response levels will be filtered to ‘yes’ or equivalent. ‘yes’ will be a specifiable argument, e.g. could be ‘mentioned’.
For simplicity, I’ll assume binaries be coded consistently, e.g. people don’t feed in a combination of yes/no and mentioned/not mentioned questions.
It will replace variable level == ‘yes’ with the right hand part of the stem.
Variable name will be reduced to the stem that is consistent across all variables in that set. Not dealt yet with the possibility that there is no consistent stem.
Base description will be updated to have a single base description for the variable as a whole, using the left hand part of the stem as the variable label.
This new base description will be silently added to the object with base description in it, in these trials that is example_of_base_information.
Should I then drop duplicates from the base description info? Probably, yes.

8.2.3 Convenience function to reduce variable names to a common stem
This takes a vector of variable names and returns a single character value with the common parts of the strings in that vector, assuming there is one.

# Example vector of multi-coded variable names
vars <- c("Q1_OptionA", "Q1_OptionB", "Q1_OptionC", "Q1_OptionD", "Q1_OptionE")

# Find longest common prefix
common_prefix <- function(x) {
  split_names <- strsplit(x, "")
  min_length <- min(lengths(split_names))
  prefix <- character(0)
  for (i in seq_len(min_length)) {
    chars <- sapply(split_names, `[`, i)
    if (length(unique(chars)) == 1) {
      prefix <- c(prefix, chars[1])
    } else {
      break
    }
  }
  paste0(prefix, collapse = "")
}

write_function(common_prefix, folder = "Scripts")

common_prefix(vars)

8.2.4 Intial variable screening
The first stage narrows the data frame received from calc_stats down to suitable rows:

stat must equal “perc” or “count”,

o_lab must contain “:”,

The outcome variable must contain either 1 or 2 levels,

Those levels must include the relevant value, for now “yes”. Could be user specified.



For these rows of data it them creates a variable called left_stem, which contains the values on the left hand side of “:”. This will be the variable label for the new multicode variable.



There must be more than one variable with a consistent left_stem value.

The base value must be the same within unique values of left_stem.

The resulting output is a dataframe with only the relevant rows of data from the output of calc_stats.

multis <- trial2 %>% 
  filter(stat == "perc" | stat == "count") %>% # Multicodes relevant only for categorical data
  filter(grepl(": ", o_lab)) %>% # Label must contain ": "
  group_by(across(contains(c("cross_break", "p_cat"))), outcome) %>% # Group by outcome variable
  mutate(lev_num = max(row_number())) %>% # Count number of levels in each variable
  group_by(outcome) %>% 
  mutate(lev_relevant = case_when(any(o_cat == "Yes") ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)) %>% # Any of variable's levels equal yes? 
  filter(
    lev_num <= 2 & # Only use variables with 1 or 2 levels
    lev_relevant == 1 # Only use variables with a relevant level, here 'yes'
    )  %>% 
  mutate(
    left_stem = str_split_i(o_lab, ": ", 1) # Create left variable label stem 
    ) %>% 
  group_by(across(contains(c("crossbreak", "p_cat"))), left_stem) %>% # Group by predictors and left stem
  mutate(
    stem_count = n_distinct(outcome), # number of different variables with that variable stem 
    base_count = n_distinct(base) # Number of unique values in base
    ) %>% 
  filter(stem_count > 1) %>% # Only use variables where right stem recurs more than once
  filter(base_count == 1)  # Only use variables where base is unique within left_stem

# Loop over each unique value of 'left_stem2'
result <- map(unique_stems, function(stem) {

  multis2 <- multis %>% 
    filter(left_stem2 == stem) 
  
  # Save the original variable label from the first row (for later use)
  old_variable_label <- multis2$o_lab[1]
  
  # Step 1: Create a 'right_stem' by splitting 'o_lab' on ": " and taking the second part
  # Step 2: Replace 'o_lab' with the value of 'left_stem'
  multis2 <- multis2 %>%
    mutate(
      right_stem = str_split_i(o_lab, ": ", 2), 
      o_lab = left_stem
    ) %>% 
    # Step 3: Keep only rows where 'o_cat' == "Yes"
    filter(o_cat == "Yes") %>% 
    # Step 4: Replace 'o_cat' with 'right_stem' values, and shorten 'outcome' to its common prefix
    mutate(
      o_cat = right_stem, 
      outcome = common_prefix(outcome)
    ) 
  
  # Get the unique new variable name
  new_variable_name <- multis2$outcome %>% unique()
  # Get the unique new variable label
  new_variable_label <- multis2$o_lab %>% unique
  # Name the label vector with the new variable name
  names(new_variable_label) <- new_variable_name
  
  # Get the existing base description from the first row
  existing_base_description <- multis2$base_description[1]
  
  # If the base description contains " X ", split it into two parts
  if(str_detect(existing_base_description, " X ")){
    existing_base_description_2 <- str_split(existing_base_description, " X ") %>% unlist
  } else {
    # Otherwise, keep it as is
    existing_base_description_2 <- existing_base_description
  }
  
  # Create a logical index for which part(s) match the old variable label
  index <- str_detect(existing_base_description_2, old_variable_label)
  reverse_index <- !str_detect(existing_base_description_2, old_variable_label)
  
  # Extract the matching part(s) and remove anything after ":- "
  existing_base_description_3 <- existing_base_description_2[index] %>% str_split_i(., ":- ", 1)
  
  # Create a revised base label by appending the new variable label
  revised_base_label <- paste0(existing_base_description_3, ":- ", new_variable_label)
  names(revised_base_label) <- new_variable_name
  
  # If the base description originally had " X ", reassemble with the unchanged part(s)
  if(str_detect(existing_base_description, " X ")){
    remainder_of_base_description <- existing_base_description_2[reverse_index] 
    revised_base_description <- paste(
      revised_base_label, 
      remainder_of_base_description, 
      sep = " X ")
  } else {
    revised_base_description <- revised_base_label
  }
  
  # Update 'base_description' in the filtered dataset
  multis2 <- multis2 %>% mutate(base_description = revised_base_description)
  
  # Logical test: stop execution if the new variable name already exists in 'example_of_base_information2'
  if (new_variable_name %in% names(example_of_base_information2)) {
    stop("Error: New multicode variable name already in data.")
  } 
  
  # Return a list containing:
  # 1. The updated 'multis2' dataframe
  # 2. The revised base label
  # 3. The new variable label
  return(list(multis2, revised_base_label, new_variable_label))
  
})

convert_multicodes <- function(
  data, 
  base_info = NULL, 
  keep = "Yes"){
  
  if(!is.null(base_info)){base_info_name_as_string <- deparse(substitute(base_info))}
  
  multis <- data %>% 
    filter(stat == "perc" | stat == "count" | stat == "w_count" | stat == "w_perc") %>% # Multicodes relevant only for categorical data
    filter(grepl(": ", o_lab)) %>% # Label must contain ": "
    
    # Count number of levels in each variable
    group_by(across(contains(c("cross_break", "p_cat"))), outcome) %>% # Group by outcome variable + crossbreak set + levels
    mutate(lev_num = max(row_number())) %>% 
    
    # Any of variable's levels equal yes?
    group_by(outcome) %>% 
    mutate(lev_relevant = case_when(any(o_cat == "Yes") ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)) %>%  
    
    # filter non-relevant variables
    filter(
      lev_num <= 2 & # Only use variables with 1 or 2 levels
      lev_relevant == 1 # Only use variables with a relevant level, here 'yes'
      )  %>% 
    mutate(
      left_stem = str_split_i(o_lab, ": ", 1) # Create left variable label stem 
      ) %>% 
    group_by(across(contains(c("crossbreak", "p_cat"))), left_stem) %>% # Group by predictors and left stem
    mutate(
      stem_count = n_distinct(outcome), # number of different variables with that variable stem 
      base_count = n_distinct(base) # Number of unique values in base
      ) %>% 
    filter(stem_count > 1) %>% # Only use variables where right stem recurs more than once
    filter(base_count == 1)  # Only use variables where base is unique within left_stem
  
  if(nrow(multis) > 0){
  
  # Create an identifier vector for multicode rows from: 
  #  -  cross_break (all the predictors), 
  #  -  and the outcome variable.
  # Then reduce that to a vector of unique values
  multicode_row_identifiers <-  multis %>% unite(ident, contains(c("cross_break", "outcome"))) %>% pull(ident) %>% unique
  multicode_row_identifiers
  
  # Use `multicode_row_identifiers` to drop these rows from the original table.
  single_codes <- data %>% unite(ident, contains(c("cross_break", "outcome")), remove = F) %>% 
    filter(!ident %in% multicode_row_identifiers) %>% 
    select(-ident)

  # The next step is done separately for each unique multicode set and predictor combination 
  # Identified with left_stem2, created below. 
  # Results returned as a list from map()
  
  # If the column "cross_break" exists in the dataframe 'multis'...
  if("cross_break" %in% names(multis)){
    # ...then create a new column 'left_stem2' by combining 'left_stem' and 'cross_break'
    multis <- multis %>% mutate(left_stem2 = paste0(left_stem, " - ", cross_break))
  } else {
    # ...otherwise, just copy 'left_stem' into 'left_stem2'
    multis <- multis %>% mutate(left_stem2 = left_stem)
  }
  
  # Get all unique values of 'left_stem2' in the data
  unique_stems <- multis$left_stem2 %>% unique
  # stem <- unique_stems[[2]]
  
    # Loop over each unique value of 'left_stem2'
    result <- map(unique_stems, function(stem) {
    
    # Filter 'multis' to only the rows matching the current stem
    multis2 <- multis %>% filter(left_stem2 == stem) 
    
    # Save the original variable label from the first row (for later use)
    old_variable_label <- multis2$o_lab[1]
    
    # Step 1: Create a 'right_stem' by splitting 'o_lab' on ": " and taking the second part
    # Step 2: Replace 'o_lab' with the value of 'left_stem'
    multis2 <- multis2 %>% ungroup() %>%
      mutate(
        right_stem = str_split_i(o_lab, ": ", 2), 
        o_lab = left_stem
      ) %>% 
      # Step 3: Keep only rows where 'o_cat' == "Yes"
      filter(o_cat == "Yes") %>% 
      # Step 4: Replace 'o_cat' with 'right_stem' values, and shorten 'outcome' to its common prefix
      mutate(
        o_cat = right_stem, 
        outcome = common_prefix(outcome)
      ) 
    
    # Skip base description related steps where base_info NULL
    if(!is.null(base_info)){
        
      # Get the unique new variable name
      new_variable_name <- multis2$outcome %>% unique()
      # Get the unique new variable label
      new_variable_label <- multis2$o_lab %>% unique
      # Name the label vector with the new variable name
      names(new_variable_label) <- new_variable_name
      
      # Get the existing base description from the first row
      existing_base_description <- multis2$base_description[1]
      
      # If the base description contains " X ", split it into two parts
      if(str_detect(existing_base_description, " X ")){
        existing_base_description_2 <- str_split(existing_base_description, " X ") %>% unlist
      } else {
        # Otherwise, keep it as is
        existing_base_description_2 <- existing_base_description
      }
      
      # Create a logical index for which part(s) match the old variable label
      index <- str_detect(existing_base_description_2, old_variable_label)
      reverse_index <- !str_detect(existing_base_description_2, old_variable_label)
      
      # Extract the matching part(s) and remove anything after ":- "
      existing_base_description_3 <- existing_base_description_2[index] %>% str_split_i(., ":- ", 1)
      
      # Create a revised base label by appending the new variable label
      revised_base_label <- paste0(existing_base_description_3, ":- ", new_variable_label)
      names(revised_base_label) <- new_variable_name
      
      # If the base description originally had " X ", reassemble with the unchanged part(s)
      if(str_detect(existing_base_description, " X ")){
        remainder_of_base_description <- existing_base_description_2[reverse_index] 
        revised_base_description <- paste0(
          c(revised_base_label, remainder_of_base_description), 
          collapse = " X ")
      } else {
        revised_base_description <- revised_base_label
      }
      
      # Update 'base_description' in the filtered dataset
      multis2 <- multis2 %>% mutate(base_description = revised_base_description)
      
      # Logical test: drop existing variable names from 'base_info'
      if (new_variable_name %in% names(base_info[[3]])) {
        
        keep_item_2 <- which(!(base_info[[2]] %>% names()) %in% new_variable_name)
        keep_item_3 <- which(!(base_info[[3]] %>% names()) %in% new_variable_name)
        keep_item_4 <- which(!(base_info[[4]] %>% names()) %in% new_variable_name)
        base_info[[2]] <- base_info[[2]][keep_item_2]
        base_info[[3]] <- base_info[[3]][keep_item_3]
        base_info[[4]] <- base_info[[4]][keep_item_4]

        # stop("Error: New multicode variable name already in data.")
      } 
      
      # Where base description provided, return a list containing:
      #  1. The updated 'multis2' dataframe
      #  2. The revised base label
      #  3. The new variable label
      return(list(multis2, revised_base_label, new_variable_label))
    
    } else {
      
      return(list(multis2)) # Otherwise, simply return data frame, in a list so map() below will work
      
    }
    
    }) # End of map() loop
  
  # Combine all first elements of 'result' (the dataframes) into one big dataframe
  tables <- bind_rows(map(result, ~(.x[[1]])))
  
  # Skip base description related steps where base_info NULL
  if(!is.null(base_info)){
    
    # Extract all base labels from the results, flatten into one vector, and remove duplicates
    new_base_descriptors <- map(result, ~(.x[[2]])) %>% unlist
    new_base_descriptors <- new_base_descriptors[!duplicated(new_base_descriptors)]
    
    # Extract all variable labels from the results, flatten, and remove duplicates
    new_variable_labels <- map(result, ~(.x[[3]])) %>% unlist
    new_variable_labels <- new_variable_labels[!duplicated(new_variable_labels)]
    
    # Make a temporary copy of 'base_info'
    example_of_base_info2_temp <- base_info
    
    # If those variable names already exist in base descriptions information, then drop them...
    base_info[[2]] <- base_info[[2]][which(!base_info[[2]] %in% new_base_descriptors)]
    base_info[[3]] <- base_info[[3]][which(!base_info[[3]] %in% new_variable_labels)]
    base_info[[4]] <- base_info[[4]][which(!base_info[[4]] %in% new_variable_labels)]

    # Append new base descriptors and labels to positions [[2]], [[3]], and [[4]] of that object
    example_of_base_info2_temp[[2]] <- c(base_info[[2]], new_base_descriptors)
    example_of_base_info2_temp[[3]] <- c(base_info[[3]], new_variable_labels)
    example_of_base_info2_temp[[4]] <- c(base_info[[4]], new_variable_labels)
    
    # Overwrite the original 'base_info' object in the global environment with the updated version
    assign(base_info_name_as_string, example_of_base_info2_temp, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    # base_info <<- example_of_base_info2_temp
  
  }
  
  # Create multicode object to export
  multis2 <- tables %>% 
    ungroup() %>% # Otherwise, cannot drop left_stem
    # Drop temporary variables
    select(-lev_num, -lev_relevant, -left_stem, -stem_count, -base_count, -left_stem2, -right_stem)
  
  # Bind single and multicode data together
  multicoded_and_single_code_data <- bind_rows(single_codes, multis2)
  
  return(multicoded_and_single_code_data)
  
  } else {return(data)}
  
}

write_function(convert_multicodes, folder = "Scripts")

  (predictor_label <- table %>% select(p_lab1) %>% filter(p_lab1 != "Total") %>% unlist %>% unique)

  (n_predictor_levels <- table %>% select(p_cat1) %>% filter(p_cat1 != "Total") %>% unlist %>% unique %>% length)

  (preds_df <- tibble(var = rep(predictor_label, n_predictor_levels)) %>% t() %>% as.data.frame() %>% unname)

  ht <- as_hux(preds_df, add_colnames = FALSE)
  ht <- merge_cells(ht, 1, 1:n_predictor_levels)
  ht <- insert_column(ht, "", after = 0)
  ht <- insert_column(ht, "", after = 0)

  return(ht)

}

organise_table <- function(data_table){
  
  predictor_label <- make_hux(table = data_table)
  
  outcome_label <- data_table %>% pull(o_lab) %>% unique
  
  values <-
    data_table %>% 
      select(o_cat, p_cat1, estimate, estimate_low, estimate_upp) %>%
      mutate_if(is.numeric, ~round(.x * 100, 1)) %>%
      mutate(ci = paste0("[", estimate_low, "-", estimate_upp, "]")) %>%
      select(-estimate_low, -estimate_upp) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = p_cat1, values_from = c(estimate, ci), names_sep = "__") %>%
      mutate_if(is.numeric, as.character) %>%
      pivot_longer(cols = -o_cat, names_to = c("Statistic", "heading"), names_sep = "__") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = heading, values_from = value) %>%
      select(-Statistic) %>%
      add_row() %>%
      add_row(.before = 1) %>%
      add_row(.before = 1) %>%
      mutate(
        across(-1, ~case_when(row_number() == 1 ~ "%", TRUE ~ .x)),
        across(1, ~case_when(row_number() == 2 ~ outcome_label, TRUE ~ .x))
      )
  
  bases <-
  tbl %>%
  select(p_cat1, base) %>%
  unique() %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = p_cat1, values_from = base, values_fn = paste0) %>%
  mutate(o_cat = "Unweighted base", .before = 1)

  bind_rows(values, bases) %>%
    rename("Variables" = o_cat) %>%
    as_hux() %>%
    rbind(top_of_table, .) 

}
